correctness.rationale: For a current interval gap z, two independent Bernoulli(q(z)) decisions yield idle probability (1−q)², one-sided 2q(1−q) and both q². Condition on non-idle round: stop probability s=q/(2−q), otherwise fair left/right halving. At depth k each 2^k dyadic subinterval equally likely with survival S_k, giving atom S_k s_k/2^k. Since s_k≥s_0>0, eventual absorption a.s., finite moments and stagewise geometric holding times E[T]=ΣS_k/h_k; midpoint-grid variance d²(1−4^{−k})/12. As ε↓0 fixed β,d, every fixed-depth stopping mass tends zero, and coupling dyadic midpoint to a uniform sample of its interval gives the weak uniform limit; each ε law has countable support, so TV=1. Initial holding mean 1/h0 dominates: later stages bounded by O(log_2(d/ε)/h1), exponentially smaller, yielding limit e^{−βd/ε}E[T]=1/[2(1+e^β)]. Independently computed rational dyadic probabilities through depth8 and high-precision prefactor across four ε values.
residual_risks: Claim only for exactly two agents, independent directed choices and simultaneous pre-update opinions; many-agent networks do not share exact stopping law.
Finite calculation of truncated sums used only as cross-check, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Output law and completion time are natural exact observables of a defined stochastic social-influence model. A countably atomic consensus law approaches uniform weakly but remains maximally distant in total variation; the sharp exponential waiting time reconciles extremely slow practical clustering with almost-sure agreement. This is more than the trivial two-agent eventual-consensus claim.
residual_risks: Exact inference relevance depends on assumptions of model; no extension claimed to empirical social networks.

final_claim: In two-agent independent directed logistic fuzzy selection with synchronous midpoint averaging, exact consensus occurs at dyadic midpoints with masses S_k s_k/2^k; its distribution is purely atomic for all ε>0 but tends weakly to Uniform[a,b] as ε→0 with TV distance identically one; expected round count has sharp exponential prefactor 1/[2(1+e^β)].
